sections.h2: Which two offices in Bloomfield deal with my tax bill?
sections.html:
The Assessor lists and values property. The Collector of Revenue mails the bills and takes the money. Both keep an address on South Prairie Street in the county's government building.

  • Collector of Revenue: 401 S. Prairie St, P.O. Box 80, Bloomfield, MO 63825; (573) 568-3327; staffed weekdays from half past eight until half past four, and shut on state and federal holidays.
  • Assessor: 401 South Prairie, P.O. Box 307, Bloomfield, MO 63825; (573) 568-3163. The office site offers real estate and personal property lookups by account number, name or address.

Stoddard County fills the southeast corner of Missouri, with 823 square miles of land. Bloomfield is the seat and Dexter the largest city; Advance, Bell City, Bernie, Dudley, Essex and Puxico are the other incorporated cities, per the county's Wikipedia article. A slice of Mingo National Wildlife Refuge falls inside the line.

sections.h2: When does the Collector expect payment?
sections.html:
Payment opens November 1 and the deadline is December 31. Bills are printed once the County Clerk hands over the tax books in the fall, and they reach mailboxes in November.

After the deadline, extra charges land on the first day of each month, with the amounts shown on your statement. The Collector's FAQ says a check in the mail must bear a U.S. Postal Service postmark dated inside the month, because a payment that falls short of the added penalties is returned. A bill that never arrived does not erase the penalty.

The Collector's website looks up a bill by owner name, parcel number, property address or account number, and shows payment history. You can pay with cash at the counter, a personal check, a money order or a cashier's check, or by card on the website or by phone, where a convenience fee applies. The drop box by the entrance to the government building is open around the clock, yet a late check left there without the penalty comes back to you. The resources page adds that tax paid out of a mortgage escrow account will not appear in the online database.

sections.h2: Is a monthly plan available for the real estate bill?
sections.html:
Yes. The county has run an installment plan since the 2010 tax year. It starts from last year's real estate payment, divides it by eleven, and collects ten equal pieces, then the actual balance as the eleventh. The program page says money leaves a checking or savings account automatically, on the 5th or the 20th.

  • You cannot join while any real estate tax is past due.
  • A parcel whose tax runs through a mortgage escrow is not eligible.
  • A missed withdrawal can end the plan, and any amount left unpaid at year end draws the usual penalties.

sections.h2: Can an older homeowner freeze the bill?
sections.html:
A homestead credit exists. As of 2024, a county resident who is 62 or older on January 1, owns the home and lives in it can lock in the real estate tax on that home. The credit's page stresses that it does not exempt you from tax. You still pay a bill, just a frozen one.

First-time filers have from January 1 to June 30. Renewal paperwork is mailed beginning February 1 and is also due June 30. A notary must witness the first application, and the license or state ID has to show the home address. The homestead covers a primary residence on up to five acres, which leaves out barns, commercial ground and farmland.

The page also addresses new construction and additions. Ask the Collector at (573) 568-3327 how a sale or a remodel would affect your frozen base year before you list.

sections.h2: Where do I turn if the assessed value looks too high?
sections.html:
Call the Assessor at (573) 568-3163 and ask for this year's Board of Equalization filing date. At the board, RSMo 138.060 removes any presumption that the assessor is right. In a county of this type the assessor must carry the burden of proof when a parcel's assessed value climbed 15% or more from the prior assessment, unless new construction or improvement explains the jump.

Paying while you contest follows RSMo 139.031. The whole bill is due before delinquency, along with a written statement of your grounds delivered to the Collector. Circuit court suit for recovery has to begin within 90 days of that protest.

sections.h2: What about tax certificates and closing day?
sections.html:
Land with unpaid tax may be offered for sale on the fourth Monday in August, according to RSMo 140.150. The collector first mails a letter to the record owner. When the assessed value is above $1,000, a second letter goes out by certified mail. Notices of delinquent tax certificate sales appear on the Collector's site.

At closing, the Collector's FAQ gives the working rule: taxes ride with the land, not the owner. The statement is passed to the buyer, and buyer and seller agree who pays what when the bill comes due. Buyers are expected to learn the tax status before they buy, so a title company will probably ask for a payoff or a proration. Missouri's Form MO-PTC is a separate state refund claim for some seniors, disabled owners and renters, and the Department of Revenue decides who qualifies.

sections.h2: How strong is the local economy and housing market?
sections.html:
The job base is modest. QuickFacts counts 644 employer establishments in 2023, with total employment of 8,455 and a yearly payroll of about $389 million. Retail sales in 2022 were $572,476,000, or $20,165 per resident.

About 56.7% of residents aged 16 and up are in the labor force, and the typical commute is 23.1 minutes. Among adults 25 and older, 83.7% finished high school and 16.7% hold a bachelor's degree or more. Owners with a mortgage report monthly costs of $1,110 in the middle, and those without one report $443. For the current levy on a specific parcel, read the rate lines on the tax statement or ask the Collector, since the online levy page is an archive that stops at 2022.

The county holds 11,585 households of about 2.42 people each, and 21.5% of residents are 65 or older. Broadband subscriptions reach 86.9% of households. Prices run far below the $276,800 figure for St. Louis County. The Census table puts the middle owner-reported home value at $143,300 for 2020 to 2024, with owners living in 71.8% of homes.

faqs.q: Where is Stoddard County property tax paid?
faqs.a: At the Collector of Revenue, 401 S. Prairie St in Bloomfield, by mail to P.O. Box 80, Bloomfield, MO 63825, or online through the Collector's website.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay without penalty?
faqs.a: December 31. Collection begins November 1, and extra charges start accruing on the first of each month once the deadline has passed.

faqs.q: Is there a way to spread the bill over the year?
faqs.a: Yes, for real estate tax only. Ten equal monthly withdrawals are followed by a final payment of the balance. Past-due accounts and escrowed parcels cannot join.

faqs.q: Which party pays the tax at a sale?
faqs.a: Buyer and seller decide that at closing. The Collector says the statement should go to the buyer and that taxes stay with the property.

faqs.q: What age qualifies for the homestead freeze?
faqs.a: Sixty-two on January 1, plus ownership and primary residence of the home. New applications are accepted from January 1 through June 30.
